text:
jordana: Folks — sketching a compact proposal for routing + variant failover that encodes customer tier and regional constraints. trying to keep console UX simple.

mike: TL;DR of goals?

jordana: 1) Enterprise gets highest-accuracy variant unless latency/regional capacity forces fallback. 2) Pro gets balanced quality/cost (prefer quantized L2 unless cold). 3) Free prefers cheapest variant; degrade gracefully with soft quota windows. 4) All tiers respect regional colocation and data residency pins.

tara: sounds right. how do we express priority in policy? a small example would help.

jordana: pasted a compact YAML example:

```
routing_policy:
  tiers:
    enterprise:
      prefer: [variant:fp16, region:local]
      fallback: [variant:int8_high, region:local, variant:fp16_remote]
      quota: {hard: 0, soft_window: 60s}
    pro:
      prefer: [variant:int8_med, region:local]
      fallback: [variant:int8_low, region:local, variant:int8_med_remote]
      quota: {hard: 1M_per_month, soft_window: 300s}
    free:
      prefer: [variant:int8_low, region:any]
      fallback: [variant:int8_verylow, region:any]
      quota: {hard: 100k_per_month, soft_window: 600s}
```

mike: Two quick asks: (A) what does soft_window mean operationally? (B) how do we avoid cross-tenant capacity stealing when we fallback to remote variants?

jordana: A) soft_window is a short grace period where we can exceed soft quota and surface telemetry + token burnbacks. It triggers soft-telemetry events and optionally rate-limit hints to the client SDK.
B) For cross-tenant fallbacks we add a tenant-affinity tag and a fallback budget pool per region; remote fallback consumes budget from a shared pool with stricter throttles and higher cost accounting.

lee: what about eval/regression safety? if enterprise pins a model version, should fallback be allowed to a different architecture? risky for deterministic behavior.

tara: propose: allow fallback across quantization levels only if same model family and compatible tokenizer/kv-cache. Disallow cross-architecture fallback unless tenant explicitly enables 'loose-fallback=true'.

mike: console UX note — show a single, readable summary: Primary variant / Fallback chain / Quota status. Expand for advanced users.

jordana: agreed. telemetry events we need: routing.decision (tier, selected_variant, reason), fallback.trigger (original_variant, fallback_variant, latency, region), quota.soft_breach, quota.hard_block.

ops-bot: Deploy preview for routing policy v3 at job 2873 started by jordana

jordana: also want to discuss scoring when multiple fallbacks are possible: idea is to score candidates by (priority_weight * tier_pref) + (latency_penalty) + (cost_penalty) and pick max score subject to region/policy constraints.

lee: scoring makes sense. small caveat: we must ensure deterministic ties across replicas — use stable sort by variant id.

mike: fallback billing — remote fallback should attribute to tenant with a visible surcharge and appear in usage/export. ops/sales want clear invoices.

jordana: yep. implementation plan: 1) policy DSL + console summary (2 weeks) 2) runtime selection & scoring + telemetry (3 weeks) 3) quota soft/hard enforcement + billing hooks (2 weeks) 4) rollout: flag-enabled on prod for 10% tenants then 50%.

tara: what's the guardrail for canary? e.g. if fallback rate > 5% for enterprise, auto-roll back?

jordana: propose: canary monitors fallback.rate and latency.regressions; alert + automatic rollback threshold at fallback.rate > 3% within 10m or p99 latency increase > 25%.

mike: ok. I'll mock up a concise console wire and a minimal API change: add route.hint {allow_fallback: bool, max_remote_latency_ms: int} as optional per-tenant override.

jordana: perfect. I'll open RFC and link the YAML examples + telemetry event table. Thanks all. :pray:
